newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gunman frees hostages, had letter for Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gunman frees hostages, had letter for Clinton.

text.p: A gunman who took five people hostage in a California bank released the hostages unharmed and surrendered Thursday after demanding that a letter be given to President Clinton, officials said.
Police sealed off part of downtown Oakdale, a small town 90 miles southeast of San Francisco, for almost five hours while they negotiated with the gunman who had entered a Bank of America branch.
The man, armed with a pistol, took hostage five bank employees, including four women and a man, police spokesman Darren Semore said.

A police officer negotiated with the man and 90 minutes later he released two women hostages, Semore said. "Those ladies had a letter they were supposed to give to the president of the United States," he said.
Semore said he did not know the contents of the letter or whether authorities had agreed to give the letter to President Clinton.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation's Sacramento office sent agents, including a SWAT team, and technical equipment to support local agencies during the standoff, Semore said.

About five hours after the tense standoff began, the gunman released the remaining three hostages one by one and soon afterwards he walked out of the bank and was arrested, Semore said. "Nobody was injured. Everything went off real smoothly," he said.

Local television showed the gunman, wearing a white T-shirt and jeans, walking out of the bank with his hands up. A police officer handcuffed him as he lay on the ground while another officer stood nearby holding a rifle.
Semore said the arrested man, Oakdale resident Scott Allen, 23, would be charged with kidnapping, assault with a deadly weapon and possibly other charges.
Police said Allen apparently did not intend to rob the bank and his motive was to get the letter to Clinton.

Oakdale Mayor Pat Kuhn said she was very glad the standoff had ended peacefully. "I have lived here for almost 29 years and I can't remember a hostage situation in this community...It has a very low crime rate," she said.
